text:
sami: hey team, day 2 here — trying to run terraform apply for onboarding infra and hitting permission errors when attempting to impersonate a service account. gcloud returns 403: caller does not have serviceAccountTokenCreator on serviceAccount: ci-runner@redwood-dev-ops. any quick pointers?

olivia: which account are you authenticating with? are you using Workload Identity or direct user impersonation? also which project and region?

sami: using my user (sami@redwood.com). command: `gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@redwood-dev-ops`. error snippet: `ERROR: (gcloud.auth.print-identity-token) HttpError 403: Permission 'iam.serviceAccounts.get' denied on serviceAccount ci-runner@redwood-dev-ops.`

cloud-onboard-bot: If you are a new hire, please file the Cloud Access form: https://go/redwood-cloud-access. For immediate help, ping #eng-ops with the SA and project.

jordan: i can grant the impersonation role but we need manager approval for IAM changes. @sami can you paste the exact SA and which terraform module needs it?

sami: SA: `ci-runner@redwood-dev-ops`. Terraform module: `infra/gcp/pubsub` (the CI job needs to create service accounts and set iam bindings). also getting a separate region error when enabling eu-west1 resources — project region seems restricted.

ops-anna: quick check — the project is under billing account `BA-12345-eu` but it's currently linked to the org folder for us-east by mistake. that explains the region/quota mismatch. i can do two things: 1) grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on that SA to your user temporarily, and 2) open a billing migration request for you to move the project to the EU billing folder. do you have a JIRA for the migration?

sami: no jira yet, i can open one. also terraform plan shows another error: `google_service_account_iam_member.ci: Error: Error setting IAM policy: googleapi: Error 403: The caller does not have permission 'resourcemanager.projects.get', forbidden`. not sure why resourcemanager perms are missing.

jordan: that error means your user is missing `roles/resourcemanager.projectViewer` or similar. i'll scope the fix: grant `resourcemanager.projectViewer` + `iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` limited to that SA so we don't give broad admin perms. run this command to double-check bindings: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-dev-ops --flatten='bindings[].members' --format='table(bindings.role)' | grep serviceAccountTokenCreator`. also paste the exact terraform plan output if it still errors.

ops-anna: giving updates — i've granted `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on `ci-runner@redwood-dev-ops` to `sami@redwood.com` and `roles/resourcemanager.projectViewer` to your user for `redwood-dev-ops`. also created CLD ticket CLD-2345 to move the project under the EU billing folder; that will take a couple days.

sami: :thumbsup: confirmed i can now run `gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@redwood-dev-ops` — token prints. terraform apply got past the IAM steps but later failed when enabling a region API (quota/region disabled). i've filed CLD-2346 for region quota and linked CLD-2345.

cloud-onboard-bot: Reminder: after ops finishes the migration, please re-run `gcloud kms keys list --location=eu-west1 --keyring=redwood-prod` to validate KMS access and `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-dev-ops` to verify bindings.

jordan: note for future new hires — if you need EU resources on day 0, mention "eu-billing" on the cloud access form and include the list of required APIs (compute.googleapis.com, cloudkms.googleapis.com, pubsub.googleapis.com). avoids the temporary back-and-forth.

sami: thanks everyone — really appreciate the quick turnaround. i'll keep the tickets updated and ping if terraform surfaces anything else. :raised_hands:
